name: AssemblyForNeovim
works_with: Neovim with lazy.nvim; C, C++ and Rust
short: A Neovim plugin that shows the assembly for your C, C++ or Rust code in a floating window.
what: AssemblyForNeovim compiles the function under your cursor, or the lines you select, and shows the assembly in a floating window. In that window you can change the `-O` level and rerun. It uses `compile_commands.json` if it finds one.
who: C, C++ and Rust programmers who use Neovim and want to check what the compiler produces without leaving the editor. Everyone else can skip it.
needs: Neovim with the lazy.nvim plugin manager

steps.title: Show a function's assembly
steps.text: Press `<leader>a` in normal mode for the function under the cursor, or in visual mode for the selected lines. `:'<,'>Asm` also works.

steps.title: Work in the window
steps.text: `+` and `-` change the `-O` level, `R` reruns and `q` closes.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Put the cursor in a function and press `<leader>a`, then press `+` to see how a higher `-O` level changes the output.

watch: It runs your compiler on your code to produce the assembly.
